 Blue Jays claim Christian Cairo off waivers from Dodgers
 Cairo was on Dodgers 40-man roster for 8 days
 by Eric Stephen Nov 19, 2026, 9:02 PM UTC Facebook 
 Link 
 The Toronto Blue Jays on Thursday claimed infielder/outfielder Christian Cairo off waivers from the Dodgers, ending his week and a half with the team.
 Cairo was designated for assignment on November 17 as the Dodgers added four pitching prospects to the 40-man roster . His time on the 40-man roster totaled eight days, as he was claimed off waivers from the New York Mets on November 9 .
 The utility player posted a career-best 17.5-percent walk rate in Triple-A in 2026, with his 92 walks split among his time at Lehigh Valley (128 games in the Philadelphia Phillies system) and Syracuse (2 games, Mets). Cairo hit .230/.381/.300 with a 95 wRC+, four home runs, 15 doubles, and 25 stolen bases in 37 attempts.
 Cairo, who turns 26 in June, has started games at shortstop, third base, and second base plus all three outfielder position in each of the last three minor league seasons.
 Though he was added to the 40-man roster by the Phillies ahead of the 2026 season, Cairo has yet to make his major league debut. He has two minor league option years remaining.
 One might wonder why the Dodgers would claim a player like Cairo only to dispatch him little more than a week later. But the fact was the team pounced when Cairo became available because they had roster room at the time. Anything that happens after that can be dealt with later. And because the Dodgers won 100 games in 2026, second only to the 103-win Milwaukee Brewers, their offseason waiver position is next to last. So if Cairo went unclaimed by at least 28 other teams previously, it stood to reason that he might go unclaimed now, especially after teams added new players to their 40-man rosters.
 But that wasn’t to be, and now Cairo is elsewhere. But if you’re looking forward to 2027 season player reviews, Cairo’s eight days on the 40-man roster puts him on the schedule for next offseason.
